claims.text: A predictive simulation approach incorporating chemical short-range order can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach can discriminate structures containing percolative ordered clusters from structures that remain random.
Inducing short-range order in bcc HfNbTaTiZr promotes HfTi and TiZr clusters.
The induced HfTi and TiZr clusters form ordered B2-like regions.
Short-range-order clusters can percolate to form ordered pathways in bcc HfNbTaTiZr.
Percolative ordered pathways reduce local lattice distortion.
Reduced local lattice distortion lessens phonon-scattering effects.
Short-range order modifies the high-frequency phonon density of states.
The reduced distortion and modified phonon density of states increase lattice thermal conductivity.
Induced short-range order produces approximately a 12% increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to fully random bcc HfNbTaTiZr.
Alloys that remain more random and lack appreciable percolative short-range-order clusters have lower phonon thermal conductivity.
More-random alloys are consequently better candidates for thermal-insulation applications.
The random bcc HfNbTaTiZr baseline has high lattice distortion.
The random bcc HfNbTaTiZr baseline has no significant short-range-order clustering.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to single-phase bcc high-entropy alloys capable of forming binary ordered clusters.
The predictive approach may not transfer to fcc or multiphase alloys because their phonon-scattering and percolation mechanisms differ.
